solves: Gives the person a switch that turns a setting on or off, with an immediate effect, and shows the state by the position of the knob, with the name of the setting next to it.
use_when: For a setting that turns on or off, with an immediate effect, outside a toolbar.
Several settings stack, one nph-switch per line: there is no group component.
Without text only when the name is already in the context, such as a table cell, always with label.
do_not_use_when: In a form, when the choice only counts on submission: use nph-checkbox.
In a toolbar, among other buttons: use nph-togglebutton.
To paint the track or the knob by hand: use checked, invalid and disabled.
To hide the label by deleting its text: leave text empty and give label.

checked.constraint: The Figma property marcado. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the state by it; the piece is not associated with a form. A click, Enter or Space by the person toggles it and fires input and then change; setting it from code fires nothing. The name and the mapping from marcado are a technical proposal of P79.

text.constraint: The label, already localized by the consuming application, after the track. It is the accessible name and wraps to the available width. Without text (the Figma boolean that shows the label, off), the piece is only the track and requires label.

label.constraint: Accessible name of the piece without text, mandatory in it: it becomes the aria-label of the native button. Without text and without label, the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development. With text, it is not used.

invalid.constraint: The Figma error state, with or without focus. The track outline becomes status/error, on or off, and on focus the halo becomes focus/halo-error. It sets aria-invalid on the native button. The error sentence stays outside the piece, written by whoever uses it. disabled wins over it.

disabled.constraint: The Figma disabled state. Turns the piece off: it leaves the Tab order, does not toggle, fires nothing and stays at state/disabled-opacity. It is not the only sign: state the reason in text when there is one.

checked.choose_when: false for a setting that is off: the knob on the left, the track in color/input. true for a setting that is on: the knob on the right, the track in color/primary with an outline.

label.choose_when: With text, the default, when the name of the setting must be visible. Only the track when the name is already in the context, such as a table cell; it takes label.
do_not_combine_with: only the track without label: the screen reader would announce only switch.

unchecked.token: color/input for the track, with no outline; color/background for the knob
unchecked.changes_for_user: The knob is on the left and the track is quiet.

checked.token: color/primary for the track, with an outline in color/primary-border; color/primary-foreground for the knob
checked.changes_for_user: The knob slides to the right and the track takes the brand color.

hover.token: color/input-hover when off and color/primary-hover when on
hover.changes_for_user: Over the whole piece, the fill goes one step up; the outline stays.

focus.token: outline border/width in focus/border and halo focus/ring-width in focus/halo, both radius/full; when invalid, status/error and focus/halo-error
focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, the track outline and a halo outside the track mark the focus, without changing the size.

invalid.changes_for_user: The track outline becomes status/error, on or off; the error sentence stays outside the piece.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole piece loses opacity, leaves the Tab order and stops responding.

business_rules: The piece holds one boolean, checked. Only a click, Enter or Space by the person toggles it and fires input and then change; setting checked from code fires nothing.
input bubbles and crosses shadow roots; change bubbles and does not, as on a native control. The new value is read from event.target.checked. There is no nph event.
disabled wins over invalid: a disabled piece draws no error outline and has no aria-invalid. It is not an error case.
The knob slides by transform, never by layout position, and the track fill and outline change on motion/state-duration and motion/state-easing.
Under reduced motion the knob does not slide: it changes side by opacity on motion/hover-duration, and the color still changes.
Inside nph-field, the piece is one option of a group: nphFieldRole is option, and the field writes invalid and disabled on it.
domain_errors: invalid: the value of the setting is not accepted by the screen. The piece shows the outline; the sentence is written outside it.
ai_hints: Use nph-switch for a setting that turns on or off with an immediate effect, outside a toolbar; in a toolbar, use nph-togglebutton; in a form, use nph-checkbox.
Stack several settings, one nph-switch per line; there is no group component.
Without text, fill in label; the piece is only the track and has no other name.
Read the new value from event.target.checked in the change event; there is no nph event.
Write the error sentence outside the piece; invalid only changes the track outline.
Do not paint the track or the knob: checked, invalid and disabled draw every state.

accessibility.semantics: A native button inside the component, with type=button, role=switch and aria-checked following checked; the track is aria-hidden. invalid sets aria-invalid, which role=switch supports. The piece is not associated with a form.
accessibility.accessible_name: The label text. Without text, the label, mandatory, as the aria-label of the native button.
keyboard: Tab enters and leaves the piece.
accessibility.focus: Keyboard only: the track outline turns focus/border and a halo in focus/halo shows outside the track, both radius/full, without changing the size; when invalid, status/error and focus/halo-error. The label gets no ring. Known limit, recorded in design.md and measured in the test: focus/border against focus/halo is 2.92:1 in the default brand in light mode; every other brand and scheme passes 3:1.
accessibility.contrast: The rule is 3:1 for the track edge on the page background and for the knob on its track, in every brand and in both schemes; the test measures both. color/input on color/background measures 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark. color/primary-border on color/background measures at least 4.96:1 in light and 4.91:1 in dark. color/background on color/input measures 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark, and color/primary-foreground on color/primary at least 4.96:1. The error outline, status/error on color/background, measures 6.88:1 in light and 5.01:1 in dark. The label, color/foreground on color/background, passes 4.5:1.
accessibility.color_alternative: On and off show in the knob position, not only in the track color. The invalid piece changes its outline; the error sentence stays outside.

invalid_combinations: disabled with invalid — disabled wins, and the error outline is not drawn.
Only the track without label — the screen reader would announce only switch.
No text and no label — the piece has no accessible name and draws nothing.
anti_patterns: Using the piece in a form whose choice only counts on submission.
Using the piece among toolbar buttons.
Painting the track or the knob by hand.
Deleting the label text to hide it without giving label.
Putting the error sentence inside the piece.
Grouping several pieces in a component of its own: they stack, one per line.
